newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Rains again slow harvest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Rains again slow harvest.

text.p: Rains moved across eastern Montana and into the Dakotas and Minnesota late Thursday and Friday, stalling harvest progress and keeping a lid on movement, grain dealers said.
"This has just been a really slow harvest," a Minnesota dealer said. "They keep getting rains through the Dakotas. Every time they get hit it just washes out more quality."

Scab has been a concern for several weeks as excessive moisture plagues the wheat and durum crops, most notably in North Dakota, dealers said. Further west, quality appeared better but the harvest was progressing slowly.

"A lot of guys around here are about three to five days away from getting done with the winter (wheat) but they've just barely got started on the spring," an eastern Montana dealer said. "It seems like every time they start cutting, the rains come in again."
Bids edged higher in most areas in reaction to a 1-1/4 cent per bushel gain in September MGE spring wheat futures.
